fieldMarks: Medium tree squirrel with grizzled gray upperparts, often with cinnamon hues, and whitish underparts
Bushy tail pale gray to white-fringed
Some individuals are black, reddish or white
behavior: Very vocal: squalls, warning barks, chucks and tooth chattering, often with tail flicks
Staples are acorns and other nuts, plus buds, fruit, fungi and corn
Breeds twice a year (December–February and May–June); nests in cavities or leaf nests
Mass movements can follow nut-crop failure or high populations
habitat: Hardwood forest with bushy understorey, in rural and urban areas, including city parks and yards.
range: Eastern United States and adjacent southern Canada from southern Quebec to Manitoba, south to eastern Texas and Florida. Introduced populations exist in British Columbia, Saskatchewan, Alberta, Nova Scotia and the U.S. Pacific states and Montana.
